metaDescription: Six Euhomy nugget ice makers compared by first-batch speed, daily output, smart control, countertop size and a built-in under-counter model for heavy use.
expertTake: The Euhomy Smart Nugget 42 lb with app and Alexa control is the pick for most homes, because its claimed 7 minute first batch and scheduling make it easy to live with. The Euhomy under-counter 70 lb is the pick when a countertop machine is not enough. Skip the fastest-start claims if you are comparing them, because a 4 minute first batch is a cold-start best case, not a pace for the rest of the day.
introParagraphs: A nugget ice machine turns water into soft, airy pellets by freezing a thin layer on the wall of a cold cylinder and scraping it off with a rotating auger. The scrapings are pressed together into the small pieces people love to chew, and the process is why these machines are heavier and louder than bullet makers.

Within one maker's nugget range the differences are mostly about speed to first ice, daily volume, controls and how the machine is installed. We compare the models on those points and on the upkeep every auger machine needs, then rank who each one suits.

products.name: Euhomy Smart Nugget ice maker countertop, 42 lb, 7 min, app and Alexa
products.description:
The Smart Nugget pairs a claimed 42 pounds a day with app and Alexa control, which turns a countertop appliance into one you can schedule. Start it from your phone on the way home, and ice is waiting when you arrive, a feature that matters more with a nugget machine because the first batch takes several minutes.

It makes the same soft, crunchy sonic nugget as the other models, which cools drinks quickly and absorbs flavor. A claimed seven minute first batch is in line with the range. The smart layer adds electronics, so confirm there is a manual button for basic operation.

Compared with the 44 lb model it makes slightly less and adds control; compared with the 35 lb stainless unit it makes more. Descale on schedule, keep vent clearance and clean the bin every couple of weeks.
products.bestFor: Homes that want scheduled, remote-controlled nugget ice.
pros: App and Alexa control with scheduling
cons: Smart features add electronics to fail
Louder than a bullet or cube maker

products.name: Euhomy under-counter nugget ice maker, 70 lb per day, double baskets
products.description:
At 70 pounds a day with double ice baskets, this is the largest machine in the nugget range and the only one built to sit under a counter. It keeps up with a household or a small office, and the extra baskets mean more stored ice before the machine pauses.

Cubes aside, you get the same soft, easy-to-chew sonic-style nugget, but the machine is a different class of equipment. A built-in or freestanding body suits a bar, a break room or a kitchen where a countertop unit would crowd the space. It needs a drain or a plan for meltwater, and an outlet and clearance behind a cabinet door.

Compared with the countertop models it makes about twice as much and stores more. Clean the condenser, sanitize the baskets and descale on a schedule, because a bigger machine scales just as readily.
products.bestFor: Offices, bars and large households needing a built-in nugget supply.
pros: 70 lb per day is the highest in the range
cons: Needs a drain plan and cabinet clearance
Much larger and pricier than countertop units

products.name: Euhomy nugget ice maker countertop, 44 lb, 7 to 10 min, scoop and basket
products.description:
This is the highest-output countertop Euhomy nugget maker at 44 pounds a day. It claims fast and endless ice in seven to ten minutes, and the scoop and basket arrive in the box, so you can start using it the day it comes.

The seven to ten minute range is the maker's own spread, a reminder that room temperature and water temperature move the number. A self-cleaning cycle handles routine flushing but not scale, so descaling still falls to you. The body is heavier than a bullet maker because of the auger and compressor.

Compared with the Smart Nugget it makes slightly more and lacks the app. Descale every month or two, keep clearance around the vents and drain the tank if the machine will sit idle.
products.bestFor: Heavy countertop users who do not need an app.
pros: 44 lb per day is the top countertop output
cons: Start time ranges from 7 to 10 minutes

products.name: Euhomy nugget ice maker with handle, 40 lb, ice in 4 minutes
products.description:
A claimed four minute first batch is the fastest in the Euhomy nugget range, which suits a kitchen where someone wants a drink right now. The maker lists a maximum of 40 pounds a day and a compact body about 12 inches wide with a sturdy handle for moving.

The four minute number describes the first ice from a cold start in good conditions, and later cycles settle into the normal pace. The compact size suits a small counter, and the handle helps with a machine that is heavier than it looks. Self-cleaning is included.

Against the 44 lb model it starts faster and makes slightly less, with a smaller body. Descale monthly, keep vents clear and dry the bin if the machine will be idle.
products.bestFor: Small kitchens where quick first ice and a compact body matter.
cons: Maximum daily output of 40 lb is mid-range
Fast start is a cold-start best case

products.name: Euhomy 2026 upgraded nugget ice maker, 35 lb, dual pump, 5 to 7 min
products.description:
The upgraded model adds a second pump, which separates water supply from drain and cleaning flow and makes self-cleaning more thorough. It claims a first batch in about five to seven minutes and a daily output of 35 pounds.

The maker gives sensible cleaning guidance: after a deep clean with descaler, run two or three self-cleaning cycles with fresh water and discard the first batch or two of ice. That advice is worth following on any nugget machine. Output is the usual soft, crunchy nugget.

Against the 40 lb model it makes less but starts nearly as fast and cleans better. Place it with vent clearance, descale on schedule and wipe the bin regularly.
products.bestFor: Owners who care about a thorough cleaning routine.
pros: First batch in about 5 to 7 minutes
Clear cleaning guidance from the maker
cons: Lower output than the 40 to 44 lb models

products.name: Euhomy nugget ice maker with handle, 34 lb, 6 min, removable cover
products.description:
A removable top cover is the small feature that makes this Euhomy easier to clean than most: lift the lid off and wipe the whole bin without fighting a hinge. It claims first ice in as little as six minutes and 34 pounds a day, with an auto-cleaning cycle for routine flushes.

The pellets are small and airy, and they cool drinks quickly. A carry handle helps with moving the machine, and the output suits a small household. The scale on the cylinder is the same story as with every auger machine and needs a regular descale.

Compared with the 35 lb dual-pump model it makes slightly less and has an easier lid. Wipe the bin every couple of weeks, descale monthly and keep clearance on all sides.
products.bestFor: Households that want the easiest bin to clean.
pros: Removable top cover for easy cleaning
First ice in as little as 6 minutes
cons: 34 lb per day is the lowest output here

buyingCriteria.explanation: Euhomy quotes first ice from 4 minutes on the 40 lb model to 7 to 10 on the 44 lb. Those are cold-start numbers in good conditions, and after the first batch the machine settles into the normal pace of making about a pound or two an hour. A fast start is a convenience, not a measure of daily output.

Countertop models run from 34 to 44 pounds, the under-counter model claims 70. A household that drinks a lot of iced coffee and soda benefits from the larger numbers, but the bin still stops production when it is full. Match the output to how much ice you actually go through between refills.

The Smart Nugget adds app and Alexa control and scheduling. That lets the machine have ice ready on a schedule and cuts the wait for the first batch. It also adds electronics that can fail, so confirm that a button on the machine starts ice without the app.

A countertop nugget machine sits on a counter and is filled by hand. The 70 lb under-counter model is built in or freestanding, with double baskets and a larger body. It suits a bar or office but needs space, a drain plan and an outlet behind a cabinet.

The upgraded model's dual pump improves flow during cleaning, and the 34 lb model's removable cover makes wiping the bin easy. Every machine here has a self-cleaning cycle, but none removes scale. Follow the maker's advice to run clean-water cycles and discard the first ice after descaling.

Nugget machines run an auger and a compressor, so they are louder than cube or bullet makers. Place the machine on a solid surface, away from a bedroom wall, with clearance on all sides. A cabinet that traps heat raises the noise and cuts output.

specDecoder.watchFor: Sonic, pebble, pellet and nugget all describe the same ice.

specDecoder.meaning: The time to first ice from a cold start. It excludes later steady cycles.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 40 lb model claims 4 minutes and the 44 lb model 7 to 10.

specDecoder.meaning: Separate pumps for supply and drain or cleaning flow, improving thoroughness.
specDecoder.watchFor: Only the 2026 upgraded 35 lb model lists it.

specDecoder.meaning: A built-in or freestanding body sized to fit beneath a counter, usually with a larger bin.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 70 lb model needs a drain plan and ventilation.

specDecoder.watchFor: The 70 lb figure is a ceiling, not a promise.

howWeEvaluated.title: Speed to first ice
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared claimed first-batch times, from 4 to 10 minutes. A faster start scored higher for convenience. We treated all numbers as cold-start best cases.

howWeEvaluated.title: Daily output
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at output from 34 pounds on the smallest to 70 on the under-counter model. Higher output scored for heavy use. We also checked how stored ice is held.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls and features
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the Smart Nugget's app and Alexa with the scoop-based models and the dual-pump design. Smart features earned credit for scheduling. We flagged the extra electronics.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning design
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at the dual pump, the removable lid and the maker's cleaning guidance. Machines that are easy to wipe scored higher. None removes scale automatically.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and installation
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered the compact 12 inch body of the 40 lb model and the built-in 70 lb unit. Handles and weight were noted. Under-counter installation was flagged for space and drain needs.

cards.label: Countertop
cards.text: The 34 to 44 lb models sit on a counter and are filled by hand. They are portable and need no plumbing.

cards.label: Under-counter
cards.text: The 70 lb model is built in or freestanding with double baskets. It makes and stores more but needs space and a drain plan.

howToChoose.note: Countertop for homes; under-counter for offices and bars.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Soft nugget ice, a quick first batch and enough daily output for several drinks. A scheduling app helps.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Smart Nugget 42 lb suits coffee households best. The 40 lb model suits a quick-start kitchen.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You go through ice all day or want scheduling. The Smart Nugget and the under-counter model repay.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You want chewable ice a few times a week. The 34 lb model is enough.

maintenance.why: Scale slows the auger and cuts output. Citric acid or a maker-approved descaler removes it.
Residue leaves a taste. The maker advises two or three clean cycles and discarding early ice, and a quick taste of the next fresh batch confirms that the descaler is fully gone.
A damp bin grows biofilm. A removable lid makes this a quick job, and a soft cloth with a mild cleaner reaches the corners where scoops and baskets rest and where stale moisture collects first.

Lint and dust packed against the Euhomy vents restrict cooling air, so the compressor works harder and the ice slows. A few inches of space behind and beside the machine is the single most useful thing you can give it, and it costs nothing.

maintenance.task: Clean condenser on the under-counter unit
maintenance.why: A built-in machine collects dust behind the cabinet door. A clean coil keeps output up, and a quick vacuum with a brush head every month is usually all it takes.

faq.q: Which Euhomy nugget ice maker is best for most homes?
faq.a: The Smart Nugget 42 lb suits most, since scheduling and app control remove the wait for ice. The 44 lb model is the pick if you want output without an app. If you want a compact body and a fast start, the 40 lb model with a handle is worth a look, and the 34 lb model with a removable cover is the easiest to keep clean.

faq.q: Is a 4 minute first batch real?
faq.a: It is the maker's best case from a cold start in good conditions. After the first batch, the machine runs at its normal pace, so do not use it to judge daily output. The more honest comparison is the daily rating and the tank size, and even those assume a cool room, so expect real output to land a little below the label.

faq.q: Do I need plumbing for a nugget ice maker?
faq.a: Not for the countertop models, which fill by hand. The 70 lb under-counter machine needs a drain plan and ventilation. Behind a cabinet door it also needs air to move, so a vented kickplate or an open front is better than a closed box that traps compressor heat.

A heavier-use household should descale monthly, and a lighter one can wait two months unless the water is hard. Scale slows the auger and cuts output. Self-cleaning cycles do not remove it. Hard water is the main driver, so a household with a water filter can stretch the interval, while one on well water with high mineral content should descale monthly without fail.

Louder than cube or bullet makers, because of the auger and compressor. Place them away from a bedroom and leave vent clearance. The compressor hum is steady, while the auger adds a rhythmic grinding sound during ice making, and many owners stop noticing it within a few days if the machine is on a quiet counter.

Not in the machine's bin, which is not a freezer. Melt water drains back to the reservoir, so use it fresh or bag and freeze it. Nugget ice clumps when it sits wet, so a freezer bag with the air pressed out stores it better than an open bowl, and a firm shake before use breaks the clumps apart.
